newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia pledges not to tolerate corruption.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia pledges not to tolerate corruption.

text.p: Indonesian State Secretary Murdiono pledged before a parliamentary commission on Tuesday that the government would not tolerate corruption.

"The government will never allow corruption, let alone give its blessing to corruption by anyone. Investigation, prosecution and the trial of those accused of corruption will be implemented according to the law," Murdiono told parliament.
"It is important for us to continue to combat corruption in order to uphold clean government," he said.
The Jakarta Post on Friday quoted Indonesia's official audit body as saying its findings on government corruption were routinely ignored by authorities.

"I think they feel ashamed with the findings, but their lack of attention to our findings really hurts us," Sudarjono, chairman of the National Supervision and Development Board (BPKP), was quoted as saying.
In the 1995/6 fiscal year BPKP found 14,572 cases of corruption with the potential loss of 532.59 billion rupiah ($229 million), Sudarjono said.
But internal auditors in government offices and state companies were often unwilling to follow up the financial irregularities, he added.
In the fiscal year 1994/5, only 27 percent of corruption cases reported by his office were actually settled, Sudarjono said.
